solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Victory token number 5 for Julius Caesar

definitions.meaning: the two-finger gesture made by Churchill to signal winning
in Roman numerals, which Caesar would have used, five is written as the letter V, so it is the sign for five

explanation.surface: A Roman general's emblem of triumph, perhaps on a coin, worth five.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves define the same thing: the victory gesture, and the Roman numeral V that stands for five.
explanation.definitionFit: The two raised fingers form a letter V, the gesture Churchill made famous for winning the war.

clue.text: A little shop, a little gem

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A small jeweller's shop sells a small precious stone.
explanation.definitionFit: An opal is an iridescent precious stone, one example of a gem.

clue.text: Theirs may be set up by this here note cracking George's arty partner up

definitions.text: Theirs may be set up by this

indicators.note: cracking means breaking into, so the note goes inside the other piece
in a down clue up means the word is written bottom to top, so read backwards

parts.note: Gilbert and George are a famous British artist duo, so George's partner is Gilbert

explanation.surface: A garbled art-world tale of a note breaking up a famous double act.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is about clue numbers: 'Theirs' is the answer at 4 down, and multiplying 4 by three gives 12, whose answer is SET UP. 'here' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripling the number of the clue for 'Theirs' (4) gives 12, the clue answered by 'set up'.

clue.text: "For Auditors" — that's the point of them

indicators.note: auditors here are listeners, so what follows is to be judged by its sound

parts.note: 'there's the point' is a way of saying 'that's the point', so the spoken word is there's

explanation.surface: A sign on a door marked for auditors, showing what they are for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditors' suggests accountants, but here they are listeners. Some solvers also read THE IRS, the US tax auditors, in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive pronoun means belonging to them, as in 'a friend of them' rephrased.

clue.text: Rule fair in Dahomey that was disciplined

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the country's name

parts.note: Dahomey is the former name of the West African country Benin
OK means fair, passable

explanation.surface: A fair rule in colonial Dahomey kept people in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Something broken in, like a horse or new shoes, has been trained or tamed into obedience.

clue.text: Entertaining girl in garage is harrowing!

indicators.note: in says the answer lies inside the words that follow, across their breaks

explanation.surface: A hostess performing in a garage finds it a harrowing experience.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese woman trained to entertain men with music, dance and conversation.

clue.text: Dressmaker, prior to the end of the day, is taken in by newspaper headline

indicators.note: prior to means coming before, so the newspaper piece comes ahead of the final letter
taken in by means held inside, so the day sits within the paper's name

parts.note: The Courier is a newspaper title, as printed in its masthead
TU is short for Tuesday, a day

indicators.note: the end of picks out the last letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A seamstress, working late, ends up in the paper's headline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the end of the' gives E, which comes after the paper with TU inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived word names a woman who makes fine clothes, a female couturier.

clue.text: The order of the day on draught

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
a pull is a draught or swig of a drink

explanation.surface: Instructions for the day posted beside the beer on draught.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appeared on 1 April, when teasing tricks are 'the order of the day'. Cricket's on side, the batter's leg side, gives LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: On April Fools' Day, a teasing hoax is exactly what everyone expects to be doing.

clue.text: Blair stands by top policeman's deception

indicators.note: stands by means is placed next to, so one name sits after the other

parts.note: a super is a police superintendent, a senior officer
Cherie Blair is the wife of former Prime Minister Tony Blair

explanation.surface: A former PM's wife supports a senior officer caught in a deception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blair' suggests Tony, but it is his wife Cherie.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare word taken from French for trickery or fraud.

clue.text: Joke about the summit of Everest

parts.note: on means about, concerning

indicators.note: the summit is the top, so the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A climbers' gag about reaching the top of the world's highest peak.
explanation.definitionFit: As in 'have you heard the one about...', a single funny story or gag.

clue.text: This is a sham grid with block misplaced

indicators.note: misplaced says the letters are put in the wrong spots, rearranged

explanation.surface: A crossword grid with a black square in the wrong place is a fake.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a fake gold bar sold to dupes, hence any worthless swindle or fraud.

clue.text: Trucks back, this behind head in April Fool

indicators.note: back says the word for trucks is turned round

parts.note: utes are small pickup trucks, an Australian term

indicators.note: the letter wanted is the one just behind the head, the first letter, of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Trucks reversing behind as part of an April Fools' prank.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter behind A, the head of 'April', is P.
explanation.definitionFit: To set someone up is to trick or frame them, making a fool of them.

clue.text: Sucker slips on road very awkwardly over surface of ice

indicators.note: awkwardly says the letters are jumbled clumsily into a new order
the surface is the top layer, so the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A mug slips over very clumsily on an icy road.
explanation.walkthrough: The French phrase means 'April fish', the French name for the victim of an April Fools' joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The French term for a dupe on 1 April, someone who has been gullible.

clue.text: To maximise one's strengths, take the role of Touchstone?

parts.note: to play is to take the role of a character
Touchstone is the court jester in Shakespeare's As You Like It, so a joker

explanation.surface: Advice to an actor: play the clown to show off your talents.
explanation.definitionFit: In some quiz and game shows, playing your joker card doubles the score on your best round.

clue.text: No good way to write SOS?

definitions.text: No good way to write SOS?

parts.words: No good way to write SOS?
parts.note: an O, a nought, between two letter S's spells the distress call; the answer also means misdeeds, no good

explanation.surface: A distress signal written badly is useless.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as NAUGHT IN ESSES: an O inside two S's spells SOS. Naught is an old spelling of nought.
explanation.definitionFit: As in 'up to no good', misbehaviour or mischievous acts.

clue.text: Spooner's pronounced Scot's few as Highland leaseholders

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts are exchanged in speech

parts.note: Mac is a nickname for a Scot, plus the possessive
ten is taken as a small number, a few

explanation.surface: A Scot's handful of tenants named in Highland speech.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of MAC'S TEN to get TACKS MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tacksman held a tack, a lease, from a Highland laird and sublet the land.

clue.text: His "Me too!" may be duplicitous

indicators.note: duplicitous means two-faced and deceptive, so the letters are not what they seem and get rearranged

explanation.surface: A smooth talker's eager agreement can be insincere.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange HISMETOO; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A suave, ingratiating person whose easy agreement may hide insincerity.

clue.text: Was hoaxer (nameless) artificially fostered?

indicators.note: nameless means without N, the abbreviation for name

parts.note: spoon-fed means fed by hand, helped along artificially

explanation.surface: A query whether an anonymous prankster was pampered as a child.
explanation.definitionFit: To spoof is to play a hoax on someone, so this means tricked.

clue.text: Doctoring cocktail? Japer's up to it!

definitions.text: Doctoring cocktail? Japer's up to it!

indicators.note: doctoring means tampering with, so these letters are tampered into a new order

parts.note: a japer is a joker; the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: Spiking someone's drink is what a prankster gets up to.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange COCKTAIL and JAPER; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacing a drink is a typical prank played for laughs on a victim.

clue.text: Three times, the same group's catching this fly

indicators.note: catching means holding the answer inside, so the outer letters of the long string fall away

parts.note: a set is a group; the same word three times gives three sets in a row

explanation.surface: A cluster of insects keeps catching the same fly.
explanation.walkthrough: Write SET three times, SETSETSET, and the fly sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The African biting insect that spreads sleeping sickness.

clue.text: Strain on stage stretches lieutenant's rope

indicators.note: stretches means the officer's letters are pulled apart around the song

parts.note: Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant
an aria is a song, a strain, sung on the opera stage

explanation.surface: A singer on stage strains the officer's rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A long rope with a noose, a lasso used for catching cattle.

clue.text: Young woman one leads astray

indicators.note: leads means goes in front, so the single letter comes first

parts.note: A means one
a miss is a young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: A girl being led off the straight and narrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Going wrong or off course, out of the right way.

clue.text: Australia's top batsman is something invigorating

parts.note: Oz is a nickname for Australia
the top batsman in cricket is number one in the order

explanation.surface: Australia's best batter is a tonic for the team.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh sea air is popularly said to be full of this bracing gas.

clue.text: Big pro's retrospective means to deceive

indicators.note: retrospective means looking back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: mega means big
pros, prostitutes, are tarts

explanation.surface: A major artist's career exhibition as a way of fooling the public.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratagem is a cunning scheme, a trick or ploy meant to mislead.

clue.text: With vigour, attack fool

explanation.surface: Attack the idiot with energy.
explanation.definitionFit: In 'act the goat' the animal stands for a silly person or clown.

clue.text: One looking sheepish in the middle of the week

indicators.note: in the middle of says the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone looking embarrassed midweek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sheepish' suggests embarrassment, but it is meant literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A female sheep naturally looks like a sheep, a literal reading of the adjective.

clue.text: Mum's turning to catch foolish trickery

parts.note: mum means silent, and sh is a call for silence

indicators.note: turning means the following words are turned round and read backwards

parts.note: to snag is to catch
inane means foolish

explanation.surface: Mum is turning to catch out some foolish trickery.
explanation.definitionFit: Shenanigans are mischievous goings-on, playful deceit or high jinks.
